# Selected guarded batch codec trial

Selected 30 October 2026, before any production edit. **Implementation and acceptance are UNRUN.** Start only after this decision and research are verified on main. Source baseline remains `8b14300cf42ff9524957f7f5fb41ce7db89f4c1a`.

## Evidence and choice

The corrected native study has42 paired units across12 workloads: median candidate/accepted native SQL full-fetch/decode ratios0.9686–1.0491, no declared primary signal, all95% intervals include1; modest regressions are not excluded. A separate12-pair persisted study finds float256 query/query_json medians1.2729 [1.1439,1.3261] and1.2632 [1.1782,1.3424], about3.5→4.2–4.4ms, with all480 results correct. Unchanged-source profiles count514/515 FP reads per float256 call (2F+fixed), supporting guard/normalization contribution, not exclusive causation. Preserve both results, both native methods and every failure.

Fresh parallel primary-source research supports amortizing invariant boundary work over an already-owned batch, not skipping validation or claiming SIMD/native speedup. Read admission/revision-02 first, then batch-theory and codec-tests. The theory relies on [X100 batch-granularity execution](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/16497/16497B.pdf), [pinned DuckDB error-sensitive vector dispatch](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v2.0.0/src/include/duckdb/common/vector_operations/unary_executor.hpp), [CPython3.12.14 struct wrapper](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Modules/_struct.c), [float bit-copy implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Objects/floatobject.c), [Unicode subtype copy](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Objects/unicodeobject.c), [ctypes call machinery](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Modules/_ctypes/callproc.c) and [glibc2.41 public fenv reader](https://github.com/bminor/glibc/blob/glibc-2.41/sysdeps/x86_64/fpu/fegetenv.c). Target/continuous-control assumptions remain unchanged.

Choose **batch-only first**: a private eager carrier-to-wire conversion after a fresh full post-fetch FP guard, with shared validation and no temporary public Value objects. Defer the independent owned-buffer reader micro-optimization: isolate causal/semantic changes. Do not change fp_environment.py, native engine/binding, schemas, legacy store, browser, caps, confinement or trusted artifact policy for this trial.

## Required boundaries and compatibility

1. Retain independent public readiness/closed/FP guards and existing locks. Before BEGIN, position reads, budget/ledger/history DB work or evaluated-command staging, prepare the Query/evaluate fields into an owned exact immutable Query record. Query/str subclasses remain admitted; each of the six fields is evaluated once for the request snapshot. No original caller getter/reference is used in the transaction executor.
2. Program snapshot uses explicit base `str.__str__` to preserve stored Unicode characters, not generic str() or overridable encode. The pinned Python-client source commit83c719…/engine d54cbbe… bridge and six real-runtime probes support that bound-parameter path. Preserve native program/grammar bounds; **do not apply the512-byte EAV Value cap to programs or add a new program encode callback**. Dynamic getter invocation counts are not preserved; single validated snapshot semantics are explicit. Malformed requests are rejected before DB entry; do not claim unchanged priority for multiple simultaneous invalid/duplicate conditions.
3. Preserve exact signed-i64 valid/known coordinates and exact integer limits. Keep known_at=None unresolved until the actual transaction snapshot, including post-staging evaluation; only exact-int known_at<=snapshot validation remains inside. Run a fresh full FP guard after callback-capable preparation and before DB work.
4. After complete execute/fetch, take a full FP guard **before indexing/copying/interacting with result protocols or packing floats**. Validate the exact fetched tuple/root/row/cell containers and exact string keys before iteration/equality/lookup can dispatch hooks. Admit only exact builtin backend payloads to this private region.
5. Factor shared carrier extraction and payload canonicalization for public/private paths. Preserve every selected-nonnull/unused-NULL/tag/type/range/UTF8/NUL/512-byte Value cap/finite/bitwise-zero rule. Public Value factory/from_carrier still masks-preflight; public float JSON/store/migration/close guards remain independent. No public skip_checks option, ambient/context/global/thread-local success flag, cached control state, partially initialized Values, private object-memory reads or machine-code helper.
6. Build wire output locally, preserve encounter order and exact canonical tags/int64 strings/float bits, then take a final full guard before publication. Late faults return no prefix and do not mutate raw input. Constant batch guard reads replace O(f64 cells) reads; per-cell validation remains O(cells). Empty/no-float/tiny cases must still be measured.

## Scope and cleanup premise

Query snapshotting fixes its known pre-transaction callback boundary; it does **not** remove TypedFact/Value/command callbacks from staging. Keep those existing paths, independent public guards and continuing-supported-controls contract unchanged. Do not call the entire transaction callback-free.

A nonconforming native callee or arbitrary midcall/finalizer changing controls is outside the existing trusted-callee/continuous-supported-host premise. A post-fetch guard can reject before conversion, but automatic rollback/close under corrupted controls is not proved safe. Do not repair host controls, invent postcommit rollback or claim no DB cleanup in that case. Stronger tainted/deferred cleanup requires a separate explicit design. Normal supported-state validation failures retain whole-command rollback, retry, receipts and BudgetExceeded(committed_position); genuine no-engine persistence remains.
